verdict.rationale: Babylon.js is a code-first framework distributed as NPM packages and tree-shakable ES6 modules, so a project is ordinary code rather than an editor-bound asset. The evidence also points to headless execution through NullEngine and a server-side support page. Together these make an editor-free, scriptable workflow plausible, but the evidence never documents a first-party build/export command or a CI recipe, and the build itself relies on external JS toolchains. Missing for 10: a first-party CLI build/export command, documented CI/headless build guidance (the NullEngine and server-side pages are cited only by URL, with no content), and independent or hands-on corroboration of CI builds.
